northStar: This cycle converts level-up from a beautiful-but-inert diagnostic into a living instrument that measures, trains, and credentials engineers toward Staff/Principal — and proves its flagship claim. Three things must become true simultaneously: (1) the observatory has to feel ALIVE and rewarding — the reward loop the whole design system was built around (star ignition on mastery) must finally fire, backed by a real motion layer, so effort visibly "crosses the threshold"; (2) the flagship "Real World AI Engineering" track must EXIST — as a measured diagnostic axis, as deep opinionated content mirroring the proven General-L5 voice, and as one unforgettable, non-fakeable novel feature (a playable "30% Gauntlet" code red-team) that no learning tool has shipped; (3) gamification must read as PRESTIGE, not points — earned standing, verifiable proof-of-work artifacts, calibration-gap honesty, and boss battles keyed to real Staff judgment. Everything stays coherent with the dark observatory/instrument identity, source-pinned to 2025-2026 primary references (OWASP LLM Top 10 2025, MCP spec, Larson/Reilly, SDT), and ruthlessly de-slopped. The bar: award-worthy, obviously human-authored, and the definitive tool a senior would put in a promo packet.

items.title: Wire the threshold-crossing reward loop (star ignition on mastery)
items.spec: The entire design system reserves the --spring curve (globals.css:109) for 'reward moments ONLY', yet masterModule (store.ts:63-70) and RoomPlayer.commit→awardSignal (RoomPlayer.tsx:20-25) fire silently. On mastery/clear: route the learner back to the Star Chart with the newly-earned node animating from dim pinpoint to full magnitude — reuse the existing ignite transition (StarChart.tsx:170-177) and stroke-dashoffset constellation-edge draw (StarChart.tsx:108-123): glow bloom + diffraction-spike draw via --spring, then a single in-voice instrument-panel readout toast ('DEPTH axis — star charted. You crossed into L5 territory.') and a count-up of Signal. No confetti, no mascot, no 'Great job!'. Gate all of it behind prefers-reduced-motion (final state instantly). This is wiring, not new art.
items.rationale: The gamification audit calls this the single highest-leverage add: the app's best asset (StarChart) is currently never experienced as a payoff. SDT/overjustification research (gamification report) says rewards must be competence-INFORMATIONAL, not celebratory — the 'you crossed the threshold' readout is exactly that. Transformational wow at S effort because the machinery already exists.

items.title: Playable '30% Gauntlet' AI code red-team (the never-seen-this novel feature)
items.spec: Build a line-annotator boss: render AI-generated code (the existing gen-l5-fw-gauntlet starter already has genuinely planted flaws — SQL string-interpolation injection on accountId+summary, prompt-injection via note concatenated into the system prompt, missing idempotency guard, unbounded query/p99 cliff, a catch that returns 200 ok:true summary:null). The learner clicks the exact offending lines and classifies each (injection / excessive-agency / cost-cliff / swallowed-error) against the OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 taxonomy. Auto-grade against a hidden line-keyed rubric (reuse the existing weighted rubric shape) — non-fakeable, no honor system, replacing the discarded FieldWorkView textarea. Show an after-action diff: which flaws you missed, the exploit each enables, the layered defense. New component (CodeRedTeam.tsx) + a line->flaw keyed data model; frame in-voice as 'Cross the Threshold', never 'boss'.
items.rationale: Feature audit names this THE single most impressive add: it simultaneously fills the empty flagship AI track, replaces the fatally weak honor-system Field Work with real verifiable proof-of-work (gamification 'proof-of-work' pillar; SDT competence+autonomy), and delivers a genuinely novel assessment format. Market report 2 makes hardening model-written code (slopsquatting, LLM05/LLM06) a mandatory unit — this is the hands-on adversarial lab it prescribes.

items.title: Build the real motion layer (keyframes + scroll-reveal primitive + count-up + easing tokens)
items.spec: globals.css has ZERO @keyframes and src/ has no IntersectionObserver — the audit's #1 gap to award-worthy. Ship: (a) a motion token set in CSS custom props (--ease-out-expo: cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1) for reveals; --ease-spring: cubic-bezier(0.34,1.56,0.64,1) for reward affordances; --dur-1:120ms/--dur-2:200ms/--dur-3:320ms) and never hardcode timing again; (b) a tiny useReveal IntersectionObserver hook → staggered fade+translateY(8px→0) with per-item transition-delay: calc(var(--i)*60ms), applied to proof band, track cards, method rows, stat tiles (page.tsx); (c) a count-up hook for every mono readout (Radar % Radar.tsx:119, MeView Signal/counts MeView.tsx:105, FieldWork score FieldWorkView.tsx:83). Feature-detect @supports(animation-timeline: view()) to use native scroll-driven reveals where available, IntersectionObserver fallback. ALL non-essential motion wrapped in @media(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) with opacity-only fallbacks. Animate only transform/opacity to protect INP.
items.rationale: Visual audit: 'designed by someone with taste who ran out of time before adding life' — this is the biggest single jump from static dashboard to alive. Premium-UX report: custom easing + short durations + reduced-motion gating is the highest-signal/lowest-effort tell that separates crafted from AI-template (which uses uniform 300ms ease-in-out on everything).

items.title: Restore AI Engineering as a diagnostic axis + add 2026 'Taste/Verification' and 'Leverage/Orchestration' axes
items.spec: The shipped radar (src/lib/axes.ts axis 3) silently dropped 'AI Engineering' (design.md:38-39) and replaced it with 'Execution & Delivery Craft', so a learner can NEVER be diagnosed as weak/strong in AI — fatal for the flagship. Reconcile axes.ts with the spec and decide 6 axes deliberately (mind the radar-geometry note at axes.ts:1-2 — 6 vertices is a clean hexagon). Recommended spine per market report 1: Reilly's three pillars (Big-Picture, Execution-through-Ambiguity, Leveling-Up/Sponsorship) + restored AI Engineering + the two NEW 2026 axes the report says older curricula lack: 'Taste & Verification' (choosing what to build/reject, reviewing AI-produced systems, architectural coherence) and 'Leverage & Orchestration' (multiplying via people AND agents), both anchored on the 70/30 framing. Overlay Larson's four archetypes (Tech Lead/Architect/Solver/Right Hand) as a separate shape SELECTOR, not a score. Update Radar.tsx vertex geometry, scoring.ts axis mapping, roadmap.ts deltas.
items.rationale: Two audits flag this as critical: the flagship track has no place on the assessment that drives the roadmap. Market report 1's top recommendation is exactly this axis structure; the two new axes are its highest-impact 2026 differentiator ('a radar that only measures classic pillars will feel dated to 2026 engineers'). M effort, high strategic wow — unblocks the whole AI content investment.

items.title: Author the flagship AI Engineering track content (mirror General-L5 depth)
items.spec: The flagship track has ZERO content (grep track:'ai' returns nothing). Author it in src/content/data/ai-l5.json using the proven General-L5 opinionated-judgment voice as a verbatim style contract. Phase-1 modules (source-pinned per market report 2): (1) Eval-Driven Development — offline golden sets + CI regression + online sampling, LLM-as-judge failure modes (position/verbosity/self-preference bias) with mandatory judge-vs-human agreement validation, binary-checklist rubrics over Likert; (2) RAG-that-ships — hybrid dense+BM25 + RRF + cross-encoder rerank, Anthropic contextual retrieval, retrieval evaluated separately (recall@k/MRR); (3) Context Engineering — demonstrate 'context rot' (Chroma 2025) with an accuracy-vs-length curve, LC-vs-RAG decision checklist; (4) Agent architecture as a decision framework (fixed→ReAct→plan-execute→multi-agent, Anthropic 'least agency' + ~15x token rule) + MCP module (write a server, stdio vs streamable-HTTP, tool-poisoning/lethal-trifecta security); (5) Unit economics — OTel GenAI tracing, cost-per-successful-task, prompt caching/routing/batching. Each module ends by producing an eval suite (evals as the spine). Include per-module CBM items + a Room. Version-date every claim and pin to primary sources (OWASP 2025, MCP spec version, OTel gen_ai.* conventions).
items.rationale: Both content and feature audits rate the missing flagship track 'critical' — the product's differentiating pillar does not exist. Market report 2 is the entire buildable curriculum. XL effort caps the ratio, but market-validation is maximal and it's existential to the brand promise ('reach Principal with this alone'). Phase it behind the Gauntlet (which seeds the security module).

items.title: Boss Battles — 'Cross the Threshold' chained, branching Rooms
items.spec: A promised signature mechanic (spec §47/§55) that doesn't exist; the one piece of infra — SjtResponse.downstream (types.ts:37) — is declared but never consumed by RoomPlayer. Build a boss = a chained multi-stage Room that unlocks ONLY when every module in an axis-band is mastered (mastery-gated, not XP-gated), escalating in-voice (design review → the pushback → the 3am incident). A harmful pick branches via downstream into the consequence scenario (RoomPlayer.commit reads r.downstream and advances). Authentic scenarios per gamification report (flow-channel difficulty ~4-8% above current skill): incident-command, design-review-under-adversarial-questioning, the migration, the security audit. Rich after-action review ('what you missed, what an expert did') is the real reward. No health bars, no dragons — the boss is a hard realistic problem. Frame as the L4→L5 threshold. Need ~6 new keyed scenarios so each axis-band has a distinct capstone (fixing the 7-modules-share-room-01 gap).
items.rationale: Gamification audit: 'single highest-leverage add for prestige.' Scenario/boss-battle assessments give unambiguous competence feedback and induce flow (Csikszentmihalyi); authenticity is precisely what removes the cringe for a skeptical senior audience. Reuses dead infrastructure (downstream) and delivers a spec pillar.

items.title: Replace meaningless 'Signal' integer with earned standing + evidence dossier
items.spec: Signal is a bare unbounded int (store.ts:26-27,59-61) rendered as e.g. '35' with nothing to anchor it (MeView.tsx:34). Replace with a derived standing that maps to the profession, not a number: (a) per-axis band that rises as modules master ('you now read as Solid on System Design' — reuse the 3-band language from ResultsView); (b) an 'evidence dossier' that counts verifiable accomplishments (Rooms cleared, Field Work artifacts produced, bosses crossed); (c) tier ladder named as the craft ladder from the gamification report (Contributor→Committer→Maintainer→Architect→Principal→Distinguished→Fellow) with promotion gated on demonstrated artifacts + peer/scenario mastery, NOT point volume. Kill XP-for-activity entirely; XP formula = base_difficulty × mastery_multiplier (decays to 0.15 on repeat, kills grinding) × novelty × review_rigor. Never award for login/time.
items.rationale: Gamification report: extrinsic points crowd out intrinsic motivation for experts (overjustification); prestige comes from scarce, difficulty-earned, expert-legible standing tied to real artifacts (costly signaling — Kaggle Grandmaster, not Purple Owl). Audit: seniors respect earned standing, not points.

items.title: Proof-of-Work portfolio with calibration-gap honesty scoring
items.spec: Field Work discards the learner's actual artifact (FieldWorkView.tsx:11 answer state never persisted; store.ts stores only {submittedAt, selfScore}) — it's an honor-system checkbox, contradicting spec §53 'verifiable portfolio, not just points'. Two changes: (1) add an artifact field to store.ts fieldWork and build an exportable /portfolio view assembling all produced artifacts (design docs, flaw lists, postmortems) — client-side is fine; a senior copies it into a promo packet, the artifact IS the credential. (2) Add a calibration mechanic: after the learner self-checks the rubric, reveal the staff key and score the GAP (over/under-claiming) reusing scoring.ts:156-168 calibration-gap logic — 'You claimed 5/6; a staff reviewer finds 3. The two you missed are where the level is.' Turns a weak checkbox into a signature honesty mechanic.
items.rationale: Two audits rate honor-system Field Work 'critical/high'. Gamification report: proof-of-work portfolio is far more durable/credible than quiz-XP and doubles as an external credential (autonomy + competence). Calibration-gap is a differentiating anti-gaming mechanic reusing code that already exists.

items.title: Shareable credential — dynamic OG radar card + permalink
items.spec: No sharing/export exists anywhere (grep share|export|og:image returns nothing) — a radar that can't leave the browser has zero viral or portfolio value, fatal for a LATAM brand asset meant to spread. Encode the five placement bands (+ archetype) into a URL hash/query, render a permalinked 'Level-Up Placement' page, and generate an OG image static-export-friendly (bands packed into the hash; SVG→PNG via a tiny build-time script or client canvas). Reuse the bespoke Radar.tsx as the card art. Add dynamic OG metadata to layout.tsx. One-tap 'copy shareable link' + 'download card' on ResultsView. No backend.
items.rationale: Feature audit: fatal gap for a brand asset meant to spread. Gamification report: prestige needs a life OUTSIDE the app (LinkedIn/GitHub export) — that externalization is what makes seniors actually care. Growth loop at zero backend cost.

items.title: Make the observatory ambient everywhere (parallax starfield + atmosphere)
items.spec: The concept lives only inside the hero-viz box and two charts; 4 of 6 main views carry no observatory texture and the global background is flat #080d14 + a static grain layer with dead 0.10-opacity dots that never move (StarChart FIELD 83-85, LandingChart). Ship a fixed, GPU-cheap parallax starfield behind the whole app with subtle per-star twinkle (staggered opacity keyframes, disabled under reduced-motion) and 2-3 large blurred low-opacity radial-gradient light sources (one warm/cool source, not rainbow) for depth per the premium dark-craft report. Keep the feTurbulence grain overlay at ~4% with mix-blend-mode:overlay to kill banding. Add faint reticle/tick/crosshair guide lines at very low contrast (the instrument vocabulary). Turns the concept from stated to felt on every screen.
items.rationale: Visual audit: 'the observatory concept lives in comments and two charts, not on the surface.' Premium-UX report: layered light + grain + a single soft source is the anti-flat-and-cheap technique and the exact visual grammar of an instrument/observatory aesthetic that templates can't fake.

items.title: Interactive 'where you sit on the real ladder' comparison instrument
items.spec: The landing cites Dropbox's L4/L5 code-fluency plateau and levels.fyi as proof (page.tsx:20-22) but never delivers the 'aha' — no component places the user's own bands against those ladders. Build a hand-authored SVG instrument overlaying the learner's five band ranges onto the real public ladders (Dropbox L3-L7 with the code-fluency plateau marked as a gauge notch, Larson's four Staff archetypes as a shape selector, levels.fyi scope-of-impact axis). Hover/drag a rung to reveal that level's expectation; the user's band highlights. Ties to market report 1's core thesis: Staff+ is a change in KIND (leverage/scope), not degree — visualize scope-of-impact as the axis that grows each level, and mark Staff as a valid terminal level vs Principal as a change in kind.
items.rationale: Feature audit: 'the strongest aha the copy sets up is never delivered.' Market report 1 gives the exact source-backed ladder content (Larson archetypes, Dropbox/levels.fyi, terminal-Staff framing, the 'best senior engineer trap'). A bespoke explorable diagram is core observatory craft.

items.title: Explorable technical diagrams + reusable interactive-diagram primitive
items.spec: Diagram.tsx registry has exactly 2 static SVGs (consistency-lattice, PACELC) despite the explorable-diagram ambition. Establish a reusable interactive primitive (single React state value → SVG geometry via a pure function, Ciechanowski/Wattenberger mold) and upgrade both: PACELC becomes draggable — toggle 'partition' and watch the A-vs-C / L-vs-C branches light up; the consistency lattice becomes interactive — pick an invariant and see the weakest sufficient model highlight. Add a context-rot demo diagram for the AI track (drag context length / distractor volume, watch a hand-plotted accuracy curve degrade). Direct-manipulation, recomputes live, degrades to a meaningful static state, place numeric readouts on curves via path.getPointAtLength(). Budget best craft here — one unforgettable interactive beats ten animated cards.
items.rationale: Premium-UX report: bespoke direct-manipulation explanation is the exact bar (Ciechanowski/Wattenberger) and the hardest thing for AI/templates to fake — the site's signature, most-shared artifact. Market report 2 explicitly recommends demonstrating context rot firsthand as 'uniquely persuasive'.

items.title: Responsive + craft bug-fix pass (Nav mobile menu + logo mark, layout collapses, reduced-motion, flagship weight)
items.spec: Fix real regressions the visual audit flags as high: (a) Nav.tsx (60px fixed row, flexWrap links, no hamburger) overflows/clips at ~360px — rebuild as a responsive instrument header with a mobile menu at <720px, an authored observatory logo mark (crosshair/star glyph — currently no brand mark), and a sliding animated active-link underline; (b) proof band (page.tsx:71, hard 5fr/7fr, no media query) crushes the h2 at 360-500px — collapse like the hero does at 860px; (c) LandingChart.tsx:69-73 <animate> pulse is NOT gated on prefers-reduced-motion (violates their own CI checklist) — gate it like StarChart.tsx:164; (d) track cards (page.tsx:80/:90) render two equal tiles — give the 'Flagship' AI card real weight (larger tile, clay glow, its own mini clay/cyan constellation) so it reads as flagship, not just a border color; (e) StarChart fixed 900x560 viewBox labels collapse to ~4px on phones — add mobile label thinning.
items.rationale: These are shipped bugs on the most-seen components (Nav, landing) plus a reduced-motion violation against their own checklist — cheap correctness/craft fixes that directly serve the award-worthy + accessible bar. The logo mark gives the brand an identity it currently lacks.

items.title: Deepen + calibrate the assessment bank and per-module content
items.spec: The bank is 36 items (7/axis) with 18 orphans referenced by no module retrieval — too small to support the theta+SEM/provisional-flag machinery types.ts:106-119 promises. Author to ~15-20 items/axis against the proven CBM template (distractors = named misconceptions with per-option rationales) and wire every diagnostic item to a module retrieval set so orphans become learning hooks. Fill absent Staff-critical domains the audit lists: data modeling/schema evolution, API/contract versioning, migrations at scale, testing strategy, cost/capacity, on-call/incident depth. Give each module its own Room (fixing 7-share-room-01). Mechanical authoring against a working template, not new design.
items.rationale: Content audit rates the thin/orphaned bank 'high' — it's what makes the adaptive MST/theta claims real rather than promised. Reliable CBM needs the item count. Enables the boss-battle and roadmap items to have depth to draw on.

items.title: De-AI-fingerprinting editorial pass + reviewer honesty + model-fact currency
items.spec: Three cheap credibility fixes: (a) vary em-dash cadence (currently ~10 U+2014 per 1000 words EN, ~9 ES — the single most-cited AI fingerprint) with a light editorial pass; (b) raise Rooms' reviewers count above 1 or reword the types.ts:47 'n senior reviewers who keyed it (honesty)' claim — single-authored keys presented as senior consensus undercut the honesty schema; (c) verify the Gauntlet starter's hardcoded model id against LIVE Anthropic docs (memory: Sonnet 5 is the real 2026 model; 'claude-sonnet-4-5' reads stale to this exact audience) and prefer not hardcoding a version in learner-facing starter code.
items.rationale: Directly serves the top directive ('evitar a toda costa que se vea AI Generated'). Visual/premium report lists uniform em-dash cadence and stale model facts as precisely the tells a skeptical senior scans for. S effort, disproportionate trust payoff.

items.title: Mark learner altitude + a research-backed norm line (no leaderboard)
items.spec: The learner's position on the climb is never marked (StarChart shows static L3-L7 declination bands StarChart.tsx:126-132 but no 'you are here'). Add a glowing horizon/altitude line at the current L-band with constellations above it dimmed/locked, so every visit answers 'how far up am I' — aggregating per-module booleans into felt standing without inventing a fake number. Separately, replace the impossible/cringe client-side leaderboard with an anonymized 'norm line' on the Radar — 'where L5-ranked engineers typically place on this axis' — from static research percentiles. Competitive signal without a vanity leaderboard; reinforces diagnostic credibility.
items.rationale: Gamification audit + report: seniors hate Duolingo-style leagues/leaderboards; relatedness/status must be peer-comparison and diagnostic, not a hamster wheel. Altitude marker gives aggregate progression feel; norm line is the tasteful fourth-mechanic substitute. Both S/M and reuse existing SVG.

items.title: Harden the mastery gate + bring CBM into module retrieval
items.spec: Mastery is granted at 90% on a plain recognition MCQ with answers revealed and no cost for wrong guesses (store.ts:67, ModuleView.tsx:113-124) — trivially gameable, undercutting the prestige claim. Route the retrieval check through the existing CBM proper-scoring rule (scoring.ts:60-81) so a confident-wrong answer costs you and mastery must be earned with calibrated confidence — the product's signature CBM currently appears only in the one-time assessment (AssessRunner.tsx:173-186) and never during learning. Surface a per-module calibration trend. Pure reuse of code that already exists.
items.rationale: Gamification + feature audits: the mastery gate is the prestige bottleneck and the signature CBM mechanic vanishes after the diagnostic. Mastery-based progression gated on demonstrated competence (not clicks) is the SDT-backed model. S effort, reuses built logic.

items.title: Personalized roadmap route + re-assessment history with radar diff
items.spec: generateRoadmap() (roadmap.ts) is recomputed only inside the results hero (ResultsView.tsx:31) and thrown away — no persistent /roadmap route, no progress tracking against the prescribed sequence, and retaking overwrites the prior assessment (AssessRunner.tsx:84). Add: (a) a /roadmap page in src/app/[locale] that sequences modules from the diagnostic, tracks completion against each named behavioral delta, and re-ranks as weak axes improve — the 'definitive guide' spine the engine already computes; (b) an assessment history array on Progress (store.ts) + a radar diff view animating between takes ('Systems Judgment: Developing→Solid in 6 weeks'). Reframe Cadence as a non-punitive 'observation log' (finally write the dead cadence.weeks[] array) — a quiet sparkline of weeks with activity, never break-the-chain guilt.
items.rationale: Feature/gamification audits: engagement loop is inert (Cadence toggle writes nothing, no return hook, roadmap never surfaced). Gamification report: streaks work only as forgiving opt-in commitment devices (Cadence is that primitive) — Duolingo loss-aversion nagging is trust-destroying for seniors. The diff view is the retention hook the roadmap engine already earns.
